narrative:
##SUMMARY##
Funding rates edged lower while bank credit expanded in early October. SOFR slipped to 3.87 percent and EFFR to 3.88 percent, hinting at cheaper short-term funding. The IORB remained steady at 3.9 percent, keeping the policy stance unchanged. Total bank credit rose to $19.95T and commercial loans to $2.96T, indicating more lending capacity. The DVP Repo Rate held at 3.89 percent, reinforcing a stable repo market. Overall, conditions appear to be loosening slightly.

##FRESH:sofr##
SOFR fell to 3.87 percent for 2026-10-19, down nan percentage points from the prior period. The benchmark decline reduces the cost of unsecured borrowing. This move points to a modest easing of funding conditions.

##FRESH:effr##
EFFR fell to 3.88 percent for 2026-10-19, down nan percentage points from the prior period. The lower rate trims the price of interbank loans. The shift suggests a slight loosening of liquidity.

##FRESH:iorb##
IORB held at 3.9 percent for 2026-10-18, unchanged from the prior reading. The stability keeps the overnight borrowing cost flat. Funding conditions remain steady.

##FRESH:bank_credit_total##
Total Bank Credit rose to $19.95T for 2026-10-07, up $57.1B from the prior period. The increase reflects more lending by banks. Expanding credit signals looser financing conditions.

##FRESH:commercial_loans##
Commercial Loans rose to $2.96T for 2026-09-01, up $24.5B from the prior period. The growth shows heightened demand for business financing. This trend points to easing credit constraints.

##FRESH:dvp_overnight_rate##
DVP Repo Rate held at 3.89 percent for 2026-10-21, unchanged from the prior reading. The unchanged rate keeps short-term secured funding costs stable. Funding conditions remain unchanged.

##RECENT##
Tri-Party Repo Rate rose to 3.87 percent, up 0.01 percentage points, while GCF Repo Rate fell to 3.91 percent, down 0.02 percentage points. Treasury General Account rose to $952.0B, up $68.6B, and Overnight Reverse Repo fell to $0.3B. Large Bank Deposits climbed to $19.77T, up $77.3B, Small Bank Deposits to $5.69T, up $13.6B, and Total Bank Assets to $26.1T, up $91.6B. Foreign Official Treasury Holdings slipped to $3.76T, Japan to $1.07T, China to $590.7B, while UK holdings rose to $1.01T; US M2 Money Supply rose to $23.34T, up $124.9B.

##WATCH##
Watch for any reversal in the downward trend of SOFR and EFFR that could tighten short-term funding. Monitor bank credit growth for signs of slowdown that would signal tightening. Keep an eye on Treasury balances and repo rates for shifts in liquidity supply.
